newsitem.title: USA: US Spot Products - Deals few, NYMEX tugs on prices.
newsitem.headline: US Spot Products - Deals few, NYMEX tugs on prices.

text.p: Spot prices of U.S. refined products fell sharply tracking NYMEX on Thursday, but differentials were little changed in thin talk as legions of traders abandoned their desks for a jump on the long Fourth of July weekend.
Little activity was expected, especially given the planned early NYMEX close, set for 1300 EST (1700 GMT).
Absolute prices fell sharply tracking a 1.70 cent drop in August heating oil futures and a 1.40 cent decline in August unleaded gasoline by 1237 EDT (1637 GMT).
"I think most people will head out as soon as the Merc closes," one trader said.
Gasoline differentials remained strong early in the day, though traders said there appeared to be few serious players in the market.

Prompt regular conventional M1 gasoline was talked between about 1.75 and 2.00 cents under the August NYMEX price, near even with late Wednesday levels, while end-July barrels were seen at about 3.00 cents under the futures.
Prompt reformulated gasoline also remained strong, with nearby barrels seen at about 3.00 cents over the screen, according to one Gulf Coast supplier.
"Nobody down here has much, and there's a couple people who need to buy," the trader said.
Activity was lackluster ahead of the holiday weekend, according to players, though prompt conventional M2 gasoline remained firm, with offers sitting at about 2.25 cents under the August NYMEX.
Low sulphur diesel for nearby delivery was seen near 0.50 cent over the August futures, near the lower end of the week's range, traders said.
Activity was muted in Midwest market, with differentials talked at essentially the same levels as late Wednesday, traders said.
"Most people are out, its quiet. I don't expect a lot to get done," one Group Three trader said.
Group Three low sulfur diesel was offered at 1.0 cents over August futures in thin talk, while Chicago material was also stable at 1.25 cents under, traders said.
Group conventional unleaded gasoline was offered at 2.25 cents over the print, a tad weaker than Wednesday diffs, while Chicago material was notionally stable at 2.0 cents over the August screen.
